domains.name: Where you are
domains.blurb: Position, heading, time zone, language and network address. Each one narrows down where a person is.

domains.name: How you move
domains.blurb: Motion sensors, pointer, touch, typing rhythm and attention. Behaviour that can identify a person.

domains.name: What is near you
domains.blurb: Bluetooth, USB, serial, MIDI, NFC, game controllers and casting targets around the device.

domains.name: What you see and say
domains.blurb: Camera, microphone, screen, speech, clipboard and on-device recognition.

domains.name: What you are using
domains.blurb: Battery, processor, memory, screens, storage and load. The hardware profile.

domains.name: What makes you unique
domains.blurb: Rendering, fonts, audio and engine quirks that combine into a stable identifier.

domains.name: How you are connected
domains.blurb: Connection type, speed, timing, protocols and headers.

domains.name: Who you are
domains.blurb: Sign in, passkeys, contacts, payments, storage and cross-site tracking.

domains.name: How sites reach you later
domains.blurb: Notifications, push, background work, install and page actions that outlive the visit.

nodes.n: Camera pan, tilt and zoom control
nodes.p: Lets a site move or zoom a PTZ-capable camera.
nodes.m: Gives the site physical control of camera direction and zoom on conferencing cameras, so it can aim at people and rooms. Gated by a separate permission on top of camera access.
nodes.api: getUserMedia({video: {pan: true, tilt: true, zoom: true}}); track.applyConstraints({advanced: [{pan, tilt, zoom}]}); getCapabilities()
nodes.ui: Chrome shows a distinct prompt when constraints request pan, tilt or zoom: Allow control of camera movements. Granting unlocks all three on that device.
nodes.ps: Stored with the camera permission per origin
nodes.dm: Camera pan, tilt and zoom settings

nodes.p: Asks to turn on the camera and receive live video.
nodes.m: Gives the site a live view of the person's face, room and surroundings. Used for calls and photos, but also for identity capture, biometrics and covert recording if the tab stays open.
nodes.ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow while visiting, Allow this time, Don't allow. Firefox: dropdown to choose a camera with Remember this decision. Safari: Allow or Don't Allow, per-site Ask/Deny/Allow. An OS camera indicator (green dot, menu bar ico
nodes.ps: Chrome and Edge: persistent per origin once allowed; one-time grants end when the tab closes. Firefox: remembered only if ticked. Safari: per session by default, reasks after the page is left.
nodes.rv: Padlock icon, Site settings, OS camera privacy settings; track.stop() ends capture; Permissions API 'change' event.
nodes.du: continuous at the camera frame rate

nodes.n: Captured Surface Control (scroll and zoom the shared tab)
nodes.p: Lets an app scroll and zoom the tab it is capturing.
nodes.m: Gives a meeting app remote scroll and zoom of the person's own shared tab. Needs a separate prompt because it is a control action on top of a view.
nodes.api: CaptureController.sendWheel(), setZoomLevel(), getZoomLevel(), oncapturedzoomchange; permission captured-surface-control
nodes.ui: A permission prompt appears when the controller is first used, only if the captured surface is a same-site tab.
nodes.ps: Tied to the capture session
nodes.rv: Stops with the capture or by revoking in Site settings
nodes.dm: Wheel and zoom control of the captured tab

nodes.p: Asks to record or stream a screen, window or browser tab.
nodes.m: Gives the site a live copy of whatever the person picks: their whole screen, an app window, or a tab. Can expose private messages, tabs and credentials visible on screen.
nodes.api: navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({video, audio, preferCurrentTab, selfBrowserSurface, systemAudio, surfaceSwitching, monitorTypeSurfaces, controller})
nodes.ui: Browser-drawn chooser every time: Chrome tab, window, entire screen tabs; Share audio checkbox; Firefox and Safari simple list. No stored grant: each call prompts. Indicator bar Stop sharing stays visible while active.
nodes.ps: None: every call needs a fresh gesture and picker choice
nodes.rv: Stop sharing button, closing the shared surface, or track.stop()
nodes.dm: Video (and optional audio) of the chosen surface
nodes.du: continuous, frame rate up to about 30 fps default

nodes.p: Lists camera, microphone and speaker counts; names only after permission.
nodes.m: Reveals how many cameras, mics and speakers exist (before consent, labels empty), and device names after consent. Counts and kinds are a mild fingerprint and show setup type.
nodes.ui: No prompt for the counts; labels appear once the origin has an active camera or microphone grant.
nodes.ps: Per origin once permitted
nodes.dm: Devices with kind, deviceId, groupId and label

nodes.p: Records a camera, mic or screen stream to a file in the page.
nodes.m: Turns a live stream into stored audio or video. Needs a stream the person already allowed; the point is the site can keep a copy, upload it, or hold it in memory.
nodes.ui: No prompt of its own; permission comes from the source stream.
nodes.ps: Follows the stream grant
nodes.rv: Stop the tracks or stop the recorder
nodes.du: every timeslice ms (default 0, one blob at stop)

nodes.p: Asks to turn on the microphone and receive live audio.
nodes.m: Gives the site live sound from the room: voice, background talk, ambient noise. Used for calls and dictation; also usable for voice biometrics or covert listening if the tab stays open.
nodes.ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow while visiting, Allow this time, Don't allow. Firefox: device chooser plus Remember. Safari: Allow or Don't Allow. Tab shows a recording icon (red dot) while active.
nodes.ps: Chrome and Edge: persistent per origin until reset; Safari and Firefox: per session unless remembered.
nodes.rv: Padlock icon, Site settings, OS microphone privacy settings; track.stop(); tab audio indicator.

nodes.p: Pops a video into a small floating window above other apps.
nodes.m: Floats a video over other apps; with camera access, auto PiP can keep a video call visible when the person switches tabs. Chrome gives a separate prompt for camera-based auto PiP.
nodes.ui: Manual PiP needs a click; Chrome 134+ auto PiP for video call sites is gated by the camera or microphone grant and engagement.
nodes.ps: Per origin for auto PiP
nodes.rv: Close the PiP window; Site settings > Automatic picture-in-picture

nodes.p: Crops a screen capture to part of the page, no prompt.
nodes.m: Lets an app crop a tab capture to one element and hide the rest, so a recording shows only that element. Cannot reach beyond the tab capture the person already allowed.
nodes.ui: No prompt of its own; it needs an existing tab capture stream.
nodes.ps: Tied to the capture session

nodes.p: Lets a site pick which speaker or headphones play audio.
nodes.m: Lets a site list and choose speakers. The chooser shows device names only after a pick, because output names can reveal paired Bluetooth gear and hardware.
nodes.ui: Browser chooser lists output devices; the site receives the chosen deviceId only.
nodes.ps: Per origin and device after a pick
nodes.rv: Site settings; revoke by clearing site data

nodes.p: Turns microphone audio into text.
nodes.m: Uses the microphone to transcribe speech. In Chrome the audio is sent to a Google service by default, so spoken words leave the device unless on-device recognition is chosen.
nodes.api: new webkitSpeechRecognition() or SpeechRecognition; recognition.start(); processLocally; SpeechRecognition.available(); install()
nodes.ui: Microphone prompt on first start(); Chrome shows the mic indicator; on-device mode needs a downloaded language pack.
nodes.ps: Same as microphone permission

nodes.p: A browser-drawn button that asks for camera or microphone; the click is the request.
nodes.m: Same power as getUserMedia, but the request starts from a button the site cannot disguise. Aims to cut prompt spam and make recovery after a block possible.
nodes.ui: Browser-drawn button with fixed label and icon; click opens the normal camera or microphone prompt.
nodes.ps: Same stored permissions as getUserMedia

nodes.p: Advertisers send purchase and lead events straight from their servers with hashed identifiers.
nodes.m: Moves tracking off the browser where blockers and cookie limits apply. LinkedIn matches events to members using hashed email, click ID, IP hash and other IDs.
nodes.ps: Mapping of externalIds kept 1 year; events must be within 90 days

nodes.n: LinkedIn ad sync cookies (UserMatchHistory, AnalyticsSyncHistory, lms_ads, li_sugr, _guid)
nodes.p: Cookies that sync LinkedIn IDs with ad partners and match visitors by probability.
nodes.m: Keep identifier matches between LinkedIn and ad tech partners. li_sugr (90 days) is a probabilistic match for visitors who are not logged in; _guid (90 days) links to Google Ads.
nodes.api: Set-Cookie UserMatchHistory, AnalyticsSyncHistory, lms_ads, lms_analytics, li_sugr, _guid, li_giant, ln_or
nodes.ps: UserMatchHistory 30 days, AnalyticsSyncHistory 30 days, lms_ads 30 days, lms_analytics 30 days, li_sugr 90 days, _guid 90 days, li_giant 7 days, ln_or 1 day

nodes.n: LinkedIn anti-abuse cookies (li_bapfcc, li_odapfcc, li_apfcdc, spectroscopyId, fid, fcookie)
nodes.p: Cookies that control and carry the fingerprint and extension scans, disclosed in LinkedIn's own table.
nodes.m: First party confirmation that LinkedIn collects 'abuse prevention features' from the member's device and checks for extensions. The Cookie Policy text itself does not mention fingerprinting or extensions.
nodes.api: Set-Cookie li_bapfcc, li_odapfcc, li_apfcdc, spectroscopyId, fid, fcookie, ccookie, rtc, trkInfo, trkCode, chp_token, li_cu, f_token, denial-*
nodes.ps: li_bapfcc and li_odapfcc 2 years; li_apfcdc 10 hours; spectroscopyId session

nodes.n: LinkedIn identity and session cookies (bcookie, bscookie, lidc, li_gc, li_mc)
nodes.p: Cookies that give each browser and member a stable ID on LinkedIn and on sites with its tag.
nodes.m: bcookie and bscookie identify the browser for one year, lidc routes traffic for 24 hours, li_gc and li_mc store consent and marketing state for 6 months. They link logged out and logged in activity.
nodes.api: Set-Cookie bcookie, bscookie, lidc, li_gc, li_mc, JSESSIONID, li_at, lang, liap
nodes.ps: bcookie 1 year, bscookie 1 year, lidc 24 hours, li_gc 6 months, li_mc 6 months (LinkedIn table)

nodes.n: Enhanced matching (hashed email from the browser)
nodes.p: The tag hashes an email address in the browser and sends the hash to LinkedIn to match a member.
nodes.m: Turns an anonymous visitor into a known LinkedIn member when their email is on the advertiser's form. SHA-256 is deterministic, so the hash is still an identifier.
nodes.api: Insight Tag enhanced matching: SHA-256 of normalized email
nodes.ps: Per event

nodes.p: A hidden iframe from li.protechts.net runs HUMAN's bot detection with a hash of LinkedIn's browser ID.
nodes.m: A third-party vendor runs its own behavior and device checks in the page and sets its own cookies, tied to the person through a hash of LinkedIn's bcookie.
nodes.ps: Cookies _pxvid, _pxmvid, _pxhd, _pxde, pxcts, _px<id>, _pxff_<id>, _pxttld per LinkedIn cookie table

nodes.n: LinkedIn Insight Tag (conversion pixel on other sites)
nodes.p: A script and pixel on advertisers' sites that reports visits and actions back to LinkedIn.
nodes.m: Lets LinkedIn see which pages a person visits across other sites, tie it to their member profile if logged in, and use it for ads, retargeting and measurement.
nodes.ps: Cookies bcookie 1 year, bscookie 1 year, lidc 24 hours, li_gc and li_mc 6 months, lms_ads and lms_analytics 30 days

nodes.p: A click ID added to ad landing page URLs and saved as a first party cookie.
nodes.m: Survives third party cookie blocking and lets the advertiser's tag and API tie a later purchase to a LinkedIn ad click and member.
nodes.api: ?li_fat_id=<uuid> on landing URL; cookie li_fat_id; firstPartyTrackingEnabled on the tag
nodes.ps: Cookie 30 days from latest ad click; member mapping stored 365 days

nodes.n: Matched Audiences (website retargeting and list upload)
nodes.p: Advertisers build ad audiences from site visitors or from uploaded email lists.
nodes.m: Visits on other sites and email lists are turned into ad audiences. Lists are hashed (SHA-256) in the browser or uploaded as hashes. Needs at least 300 matched members.
nodes.api: Campaign Manager upload; Insight Tag cookie based website audiences
nodes.ps: Contact lists deleted after 30 days; audiences deleted after 90 days unless used or edited; website audience windows 30 to 180 days

nodes.n: Merchant Pool device fingerprint script (Microsoft DFP)
nodes.p: Loads mdt.js from merchantpool1.linkedin.com and runs a device fingerprint call.
nodes.m: A second device fingerprinting layer, apparently Microsoft's fraud protection technology (inferred from cookie names and a doFpt call), keyed to LinkedIn's browser ID.
nodes.ps: Cookie dfpfpt per LinkedIn table; Microsoft fptctx2 inferred

nodes.n: reCAPTCHA v3 Enterprise on every page
nodes.p: Google reCAPTCHA v3 Enterprise scores each page load without any visible challenge.
nodes.m: Sends page behavior and device signals to Google to get a bot risk score. Invisible to the person; Google sets its own cookies and receives IP and browser data.
nodes.ps: Per page load

nodes.p: A single endpoint receives batched interaction and fingerprint events from the page.
nodes.m: Carries tracking events including AedEvent, SpectroscopyEvent and the encrypted fingerprint in batches, so one request can hold many data points.
nodes.api: POST https://www.linkedin.com/li/track (batch up to 29 events, 4 retries per BrowserGate)
nodes.ps: Events sent per page and on unload

nodes.n: Third party ID sync cookies in LinkedIn's table
nodes.p: Ad partner cookies (Adobe, ID5, Xandr, Yahoo, Microsoft, Google) set through LinkedIn's ad stack.
nodes.m: Shows LinkedIn acting as a demand side platform: other ad networks write IDs that LinkedIn uses to resolve people across sites. Observation data is kept at most 90 days per LinkedIn.
nodes.api: Set-Cookie aam_uuid, demdex, ID5, Xandr, TripleLift, Rubicon, Magnite, Claritas, MUID, ms_click_id, _gcl_*, ar_debug
nodes.ps: Varies by vendor (see LinkedIn table)

nodes.p: A link attribute that makes the browser send a POST to extra URLs when the link is clicked.
nodes.m: Lets a site or ad network count clicks without a redirect or script. Body is the text PING, with Ping-From and Ping-To headers. Firefox ships it disabled by default, and blockers and Brave drop it.
nodes.ps: Fire and forget on click
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.n: Ad click IDs (gclid, fbclid, msclkid and more)
nodes.p: Unique IDs ad platforms add to links so a later purchase can be matched to the exact ad click.
nodes.m: A click ID ties one person's click on an ad to later conversions, even across sessions, and is stored in a first-party cookie (for example Google _gcl_aw about 90 days, Meta _fbc about 90 days). iOS ATT era gbraid/wbraid are aggregated.
nodes.api: URL query: gclid, gbraid, wbraid (Google), fbclid (Meta), msclkid (Microsoft), ttclid (TikTok), li_fat_id (LinkedIn), twclid (X), epik (Pinterest), igshid (Instagram)
nodes.ps: First-party cookie copies, typically 30 to 90 days, then sent to ad platforms via pixel or server API
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Browser measured which ad click led to a purchase. Deprecated Chrome 144; removal under way in 2026.
nodes.m: Matched ad clicks or views to later conversions with noised event reports (3 bits click data for views) or encrypted aggregate reports. Google retired it in Oct 2025 and plans a W3C PATWG attribution standard instead.
nodes.ps: Source lifetimes up to 30 days; reports delayed 2 days to 30 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Browsers delete the stored data of sites the person only passed through on a redirect.
nodes.m: Defeats the tracker that bounces a person through its own domain to set a first-party cookie. Chrome checks about hourly and spares sites visited with interaction in the past 45 days. Safari has classified bounce trackers since 2017.
nodes.api: Browser background task; no site API (Clear-Site-Data and interaction avoid it)
nodes.ps: Chrome deletes after a grace period (about 1 hour) unless the site had interaction in the last 45 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.n: California privacy law (CCPA, AB 566, Delete Act)
nodes.p: California rules that let residents opt out of sale and sharing and that require browsers to offer a signal.
nodes.m: CCPA fines are $2,663 per violation and $7,988 if intentional or involving minors (2025 amounts). AB 566, signed Oct 8 2025, requires browsers to offer an opt out signal from Jan 1 2027. The Delete Act DROP tool opened Jan 2026.
nodes.api: Legal regime; signals via GPC and cookie settings
nodes.ps: Rights apply for the life of the account
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Lets an embedded service keep a cookie that is private to each top-level site where it is embedded.
nodes.m: A widget (chat, maps, payments) can remember state per embedding site without a cross-site ID. Capped at 10 KiB per partition, so it cannot build a cross-site profile. Supported on Chrome 114 and later; Firefox also ships it.
nodes.ps: Same lifetime rules as normal cookies; up to 400 days in Chrome
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.n: Click ID and query parameter stripping
nodes.p: Browsers remove known tracking parameters from URLs before the site sees them, in some modes.
nodes.m: Controls whether a site can read the ad click ID at all. Safari strips in Private, Mail and Messages; Firefox in ETP Strict and Private; Brave in all modes by default; Chrome does not strip. Measurement teams lose attribution where stripping applies.
nodes.api: Browser feature (no site API); site sees URL without the parameter
nodes.ps: Applies per navigation
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A tracker is served from a subdomain of the site (like metrics.site.com) that points at the tracker's servers.
nodes.m: Makes tracking look first party so the cookie lasts longer and blockers miss it. Safari caps cookies set by such CNAME or mismatched IP hosts to 7 days. Studies found it on a few percent of top sites (Dimova et al 2021).
nodes.api: DNS CNAME to a third party plus Set-Cookie from that subdomain
nodes.ps: Safari: 7 days. Others: cookie lifetime set by the tracker (up to 400 days in Chrome)
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Advertisers send purchase and signup events from their server straight to ad platforms.
nodes.m: Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Snap and Google accept server events with hashed email, phone, IP and click IDs, bypassing browser blocking. Meta dedups with event_id inside 48 hours. The person sees nothing and the browser cannot stop it.
nodes.api: POST graph.facebook.com/{pixel}/events; Google Ads API upload; LinkedIn Conversions API
nodes.ps: Event windows 7 to 90 days depending on platform
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Ad companies swap IDs through redirects so each can recognise the same person.
nodes.m: Vendor A redirects the browser to vendor B with its own ID in the URL, so B stores a mapping A to B. Repeated across dozens of partners it builds the ID graph that real time bidding relies on. Academic crawls found it on a large share of sites.
nodes.api: Image or iframe request to partner /sync?uid=...; 302 redirects; postMessage
nodes.ps: Mapping tables persist at vendors for months to years
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.du: per page view with partner tags

nodes.p: Script-readable copy of the Referer, available the moment a page loads.
nodes.m: Same previous-site data as the header, readable by any script on the page including third-party tags. Tag managers use it to label traffic sources; Safari 26 and Brave can blank it for classified tracker scripts.
nodes.ps: Per document
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A SHA-256 hash of an email lets ad platforms recognise a person without the plain email.
nodes.m: Normalised lowercase email hashed with SHA-256 is accepted by Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok for matching. Hashing is deterministic, so the same email gives the same value everywhere. The FTC stated in July 2024 that hashing does not make data anonymous.
nodes.api: Pixel advanced matching fields, Conversions APIs, Customer Match uploads
nodes.ps: Lives on platform side for the account lifetime
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: SHA-256 hex digest of normalised email

nodes.p: A one pixel image in an email that tells the sender when and where the message was opened.
nodes.m: The request reveals open time, device type, rough location by IP and a unique recipient ID. Apple Mail Privacy Protection (iOS 15, Sep 2021) preloads images through proxies, so opens from Apple Mail are inflated and hide the real IP.
nodes.ps: Fires on image load; link clicks carry the same ID
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A sandboxed ad frame that cannot talk to the page around it. Chrome is turning it into a stub in 2026.
nodes.m: Embedded content that blocks communication with the embedder so ads chosen from private data cannot leak who saw them. Moved to Deprecate and remove on Aug 14 2026; stub in Chrome 156 (stable Oct 20 2026).
nodes.ps: Per frame
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A fetch flag that lets the request finish after the page is gone.
nodes.m: Replaces sendBeacon when a site needs custom headers or methods on exit. The browser holds the request open past unload, with the same 64 KiB cap. Firefox shipped it in version 133 (Nov 2024).
nodes.ps: Until the request completes or fails
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Queues a request now that the browser sends later, even if the page closes first.
nodes.m: Gives analytics a reliable way to report at page end. The browser sends it after a chosen delay or when the page is discarded or goes into bfcache. Chrome shipped it in version 135 (Apr 2025).
nodes.ps: Sent by the browser at the delay or page end; can be cancelled by the page
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Scripts read typed or autofilled form values and can send them before the person presses submit.
nodes.m: Email and name typed into a newsletter box can reach ad trackers on blur or autofill, even if never submitted. Leaky Forms (USENIX Security 2022) found about 1,800 EU and about 3,000 US crawl sites leaking emails to trackers.
nodes.api: input, change and blur listeners; Meta Pixel automatic advanced matching; autofill reads
nodes.ps: Per event; vendor retention applies
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A browser setting that tells every site the person opts out of sale and sharing.
nodes.m: Sent as Sec-GPC: 1 and navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Legally binding opt out in California, Colorado (Jul 2024), Connecticut and Texas (2025). California fined Sephora $1.2M in 2022 and Healthline $1.55M in 2025 for ignoring it.
nodes.ps: Sent on every request while the setting is on
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Google matches a hashed email or phone from a checkout to a Google account to count the sale.
nodes.m: Advertiser sends SHA-256 normalised email, phone, name and address after a conversion. Google matches them to signed in accounts that clicked an ad. It does not need third party cookies and it works after the person leaves.
nodes.api: gtag('set','user_data',...); enhanced conversions for web or leads
nodes.ps: Conversion window up to 90 days for clicks
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Google's page script for analytics and ads; sets IDs like _ga and _gcl_au in the browser.
nodes.m: _ga (2 years, capped at 400 days in Chrome) joins visits into one user, _gid lasts 24 hours, _gcl_au 90 days for ad conversions. Consent Mode v2 changes what is sent if the person declines.
nodes.ps: _ga about 2 years (400 days in Chrome), _gid 24 hours, _gcl_au 90 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A coded record of a person's privacy choices for US states and other regions.
nodes.m: GPP replaces the US Privacy string. Its sections carry US national and state opt outs: section 7 for US national and 8 for California. Ad vendors read it via __gpp() to decide whether to sell or share data.
nodes.ui: CMP banner or opt out link
nodes.ps: Stored in a first party cookie or storage by the CMP
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A script logs where people click, move and scroll so a color map of attention is built.
nodes.m: Shows which parts of the page attract clicks, how far people scroll (in 25 percent steps often) and rage clicks. Usually aggregated, but raw events are tied to a visitor ID and can feed session replay.
nodes.api: click, mousemove, scroll listeners sent to analytics vendor
nodes.ps: Aggregate data retention set by vendor (30 days to 13 months common)
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Shared advertising IDs derived from login email so ad partners can match people without cookies.
nodes.m: A publisher sends a hashed or encrypted email at login; the ID vendor returns a token that ad platforms accept. UID2 (The Trade Desk, open source), ID5 and LiveRamp RampID let a person be recognised across sites and apps whenever they log in.
nodes.api: Publisher JS SDK (UID2 SDK, ID5 API, LiveRamp ATS) and server APIs
nodes.ps: Tokens rotate; UID2 advertising tokens are short lived with refresh tokens valid for days to weeks (verify per vendor docs)
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: Opaque token derived from email or phone
nodes.du: refreshed on sign in and periodically

nodes.p: Sites and ad vendors link visits and devices by shared IP address and basic device traits.
nodes.m: A visit's IP reveals city level location and the ISP; matched with user agent and time it joins phone and laptop on the same Wi-Fi into one household. Needs no cookie; breaks with VPN, Private Relay or mobile CGNAT.
nodes.api: TCP source address; X-Forwarded-For; WebRTC (blocked mDNS)
nodes.ps: Per request; vendors retain logs for weeks to years
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A planned Chrome proxy to hide IP addresses from trackers. Discontinued per Oct 2025 announcement.
nodes.m: Would have routed third-party tracker traffic through two hops of proxies so a site saw a proxy IP, not the person's. The Apr 2025 plan targeted Incognito in Q3 2025. Status page now says Discontinue; the person's IP stays visible to sites.
nodes.api: Browser feature (no site API); site sees IP address of TCP peer
nodes.ps: Per request
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: No data exposed by this feature

nodes.p: LinkedIn's page script that reports visits and conversions on an advertiser's site to LinkedIn.
nodes.m: Sets li_fat_id (30 days) and reads bcookie (1 year) and lidc (24 hours); can match to a signed in LinkedIn member and send hashed email through its Conversions API. Safari 27 beta is reported to classify it as a fingerprinting tracker.
nodes.ps: li_fat_id 30 days, bcookie 1 year, UserMatchHistory 30 days, lidc 24 hours
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Meta's page script that reports visits and actions on an advertiser's site back to Meta.
nodes.m: Sets _fbp (90 days) and _fbc (from the fbclid) cookies and sends page, button and form events, plus hashed email or phone if Advanced Matching is on. Lets Meta tie a visit to a Facebook or Instagram account.
nodes.ps: _fbp and _fbc cookies last 90 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Passing IDs through link URLs or redirects when the person moves between sites.
nodes.m: Works even with third-party cookies blocked: site A appends an ID to the outbound link, site B reads it and sets a first-party cookie, or a tracker redirect sets its own first-party cookie for a moment. The main workaround to ITP and TCP.
nodes.api: URL query or fragment decoration; HTTP 302 redirect chains; first-party cookies
nodes.ps: First-party cookie lifetime (Safari caps to 24 hours if set by script after tracker link decoration)
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Adding an ID to a link's URL so the next site can read it and link the visit.
nodes.m: Meta adds fbclid to outbound clicks; Google's linker adds _gl with first party cookie IDs valid for a short time (about 2 minutes). The next site turns the ID into its own cookie. Safari caps such cookies at 24 hours, Firefox and Brave strip known params.
nodes.ps: Parameter valid for the click; resulting cookie 24 h (Safari) to 400 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Events that tell a page it is being hidden, left or closed so it can save state or send a last report.
nodes.m: visibilitychange and pagehide are the reliable last chance for a final send. unload is being retired: Chrome is deprecating it with a Permissions-Policy and completing the change in late 2026. beforeunload is unreliable on mobile.
nodes.ps: Fires once at exit or tab hide
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Noisy aggregate reports from Protected Audience and Shared Storage. Removed in Chrome 152 (Aug 2026).
nodes.m: Worklet code could contribute values to histograms that a server summed with differential privacy noise. Retired Oct 2025, deprecated Chrome 144, removed in Chrome 152 (released Aug 25 2026). The Aggregation Service is scheduled for phaseout.
nodes.ps: Reports delayed 10 min to hours; budget per 10 min and 24 hours
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Anonymous tokens that carry a trust signal across sites without identifying the person.
nodes.m: An issuer vouches that a visitor looks human and later redeemers read that single bit, unlinked to identity. Chrome lists it as Continue to support after Oct 2025. Issuer limit: 2 issuers per origin used per top frame (soft cap).
nodes.ps: Tokens expire per issuer; limited batch per issuer
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Browser run ad auctions for retargeting. Retirement announced Oct 2025; removal rolling out to 100% in Oct 2026.
nodes.m: Let advertisers store interest groups in the browser and run an on-device auction, keeping the audience list local. Joins fell almost 100x per the Chrome team. Chrome 144 deprecated it; staged removal on stable reaches 100% from Oct 26 2026.
nodes.ps: Interest groups last up to 30 days, renewable
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Tells the site which page the person came from, trimmed to the origin for cross-site links by default.
nodes.m: Reveals the previous site and, for same-origin or same-site hops, the full URL including query strings. Sites use it for attribution; it can leak search terms, IDs and private page paths when sites set weak policies.
nodes.api: HTTP Referer request header; Referrer-Policy header and <meta name=referrer>; rel=noreferrer
nodes.ps: Per request, no storage
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: Origin or full URL of previous page

nodes.p: A declared group of sites that could share cookies. Removal postponed to Chrome 152 to 153.
nodes.m: Let one organisation list a primary plus associated and service sites (up to 5 associated, 3 service) that were treated as same party for storage access prompts. Retired Oct 2025 with requestStorageAccessFor; Related Website Partition discontinued.
nodes.ps: Set definition valid while listed
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Ad pixels add a visitor to lists the site owner can later target with ads elsewhere.
nodes.m: A tag fires on page load or product view and adds a cookie or hashed email to an audience (for example Meta Custom Audiences, Google remarketing lists, LinkedIn Matched Audiences). Windows run up to 180 days at Meta and 540 days at Google Ads.
nodes.api: Meta Pixel fbq('track', ...), Google tag gtag('event', ...), LinkedIn Insight Tag, server APIs
nodes.ps: Membership windows set per audience: Meta up to 180 days, Google Ads up to 540 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Safari 27 beta checks the server IP of outgoing requests and can block known ad tracker ranges.
nodes.m: Per a July 2026 code review, Safari 27 beta blocks connections by destination IP (found for bat.bing.com) and puts LinkedIn Insight (snap.licdn.com) on the fingerprinting list so it loses query and referrer data. Unverified beyond one secondary report.
nodes.api: Browser feature, no site API; blocks request at network layer
nodes.ps: Rules in a system library Apple can update without a Safari release
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Search engines no longer pass the search keywords to the site; only the engine name arrives.
nodes.m: Since Oct 2011 Google withholds queries for signed in then all searches ('not provided'). Sites see the origin google.com only and learn keywords through Search Console (up to 1000 rows per query export) or on site search.
nodes.ps: Per visit
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Sends a small POST that the browser delivers even while the person is leaving the page.
nodes.m: Lets analytics report time on page, scroll depth and exit clicks after the tab is closed or navigated away. No response is readable. The person cannot see or stop it, and it carries cookies for the target origin.
nodes.ps: Fire and forget; queued by the browser until sent
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: The site sends its analytics to its own server first, which relays it to ad vendors.
nodes.m: Moves tracking from the browser to the site's cloud container, so blockers cannot see vendor calls and cookies are set by the site's own server. The vendor can still receive IP, user agent, hashed email and click IDs the server chooses to forward.
nodes.api: Google Tag Manager server container on a first party subdomain; Set-Cookie from server
nodes.ps: Server set cookies can last up to 400 days but Safari caps IP mismatched ones at 7 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A script records page changes, mouse, scroll and typing so staff can replay a visit like a video.
nodes.m: Shows exactly what the person saw and did, including text typed in forms unless masked. A 2017 Princeton study found replay scripts on 482 of the top 50,000 sites leaking data. In 2022 to 2025 US wiretap suits grew.
nodes.api: MutationObserver, mouse, scroll and input event listeners sending to vendor
nodes.ps: Vendor retention often 30 days to 13 months
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Cross-site storage whose values could only be read in a locked worker. Retired Oct 2025.
nodes.m: Let scripts write cross-site values (for example a frequency count) and read them only inside a worklet that output through limited channels (selectURL, Private Aggregation). Disabled starting build 153.0.8001.0; code removal follows.
nodes.ps: Entries expire after 30 days, renewable on write
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: Key/value pairs readable in worklet only

nodes.p: A page can load a likely next page early, so a site may see a request before the person visits.
nodes.m: Prefetch or prerender makes the destination server log a hit, and run scripts, before any click, sending Sec-Purpose: prefetch;prerender. Analytics can over count; cookies from a prefetched response apply only on activation.
nodes.ps: Prefetch cache about 5 minutes in Chrome
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Lets an embedded frame ask to use its third-party cookies; the browser may prompt or auto-allow.
nodes.m: Used by embedded SSO, comments and video frames to regain cross-site cookies on Safari, Firefox and Chrome. Safari prompts per embed; Firefox auto-grants after 5 prior interactions and a prompt in other cases; Chrome shows a prompt.
nodes.ui: Browser prompt: allow site to use cookies and data on this site
nodes.ps: Chrome grant lasts 30 days for the embed; Safari 24 hours of use then reprompt (approx.); Firefox 30 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: A coded record of which ad vendors and purposes the person agreed to in the EU consent banner.
nodes.m: Stored in the euconsent-v2 cookie and read through __tcfapi. TCF v2.3 requires the disclosedVendors segment, and strings without it were invalid from Feb 28 2026. Consent is valid for up to 13 months.
nodes.ps: euconsent-v2 cookie up to 13 months
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Whether an embedded site can set and read its own cookies on other sites, which varies by browser.
nodes.m: Third-party cookies are how ad networks recognise the same person across sites. Safari blocks them, Firefox partitions them, Brave blocks them, Chrome leaves them on by default (user choice) and blocks them in Incognito.
nodes.api: document.cookie in iframes; Set-Cookie with SameSite=None; Secure; Storage Access API
nodes.ps: Cookie lifetime per cookie; Chrome caps at 400 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
nodes.dm: Cookie jar per top-level site (partitioned) or global

nodes.p: Chrome's interest-topic API for ads. Deprecated in Chrome 144 and being removed in 2026.
nodes.m: Gave ad scripts up to 3 coarse interest topics (one per recent week) from the browsing history of sites that called it. Taxonomy had 469 topics in v2; 5% of results were random noise. Removal rolling out from Chrome 153.
nodes.ps: Epoch of 1 week; 3 most recent epochs returned; observed topics kept for 3 weeks
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Tags in the link URL that tell the site which campaign, medium and source sent the person.
nodes.m: Lets a site tie a visit to a specific ad, email or post. Five standard keys: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content. Stored in first-party cookies by analytics tools for the session or longer.
nodes.ps: GA4 campaign data is session scoped by default; first-touch copies often kept in cookies for 30 to 90 days
nodes.rv: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

nodes.p: Reports how busy the device CPU is in four coarse levels.
nodes.m: Gives nominal, fair, serious, critical CPU pressure states. Lets video-call sites adapt, but also leaks activity on the machine.
nodes.ui: No prompt in current Chrome; blocked by Permissions Policy and requires a focused, visible page.
nodes.ps: While observing

nodes.p: Detects ad blockers via bait elements and filter-list selectors.
nodes.m: Reveals ad blocker use (about a third of desktop users) and which filter lists (EasyList, AdGuard, Fanboy, regional lists) are on. FingerprintJS probes about 20 lists; list pattern is itself identifying.
nodes.api: Hidden bait div with ad class names, fetch of ad script URL, selector tests
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Test tools leave marks on the page that a script can look for.
nodes.m: Selenium, PhantomJS, Playwright and Puppeteer inject helper properties or bindings into the page, such as cdc_ prefixed document keys, callPhantom, or names starting with __playwright and __pw. Bot defenses scan the window and document for these names. Operators rename or remove them with patches.
nodes.api: Object.keys(window) and document for names like $cdc_, __playwright*, __pw*, callPhantom, _phantom, domAutomation, __nightmare, __selenium*

nodes.p: Battery level, charging state and time estimates, without a prompt on Chromium.
nodes.m: Shows how drained a phone or laptop is. Researchers showed level plus charge time works as a short-term tracking ID. Site could raise prices for low battery or tell laptop from desktop.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Reads charge level and charging state where the browser still offers it.
nodes.m: Level and times (level, charging, chargingTime, dischargingTime) once enabled short term tracking across sites. Firefox removed it; Chrome limits it to secure contexts.

nodes.p: Checks for window objects only certain browsers define (chrome, safari, __gCrWeb, opr).
nodes.m: Identifies Chrome vs Edge vs Opera vs Safari vs in-app webviews even when the UA lies. FingerprintJS tests about 30 flavor names; spoofing tools often miss one.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A page can notice when a tool is listening to the browser over the DevTools Protocol.
nodes.m: Playwright, Puppeteer and many cloud browsers drive Chrome through the DevTools Protocol. When the Runtime domain is enabled, the browser serializes logged objects for the tool. A page can plant an Error whose stack getter runs only when that happens, which reveals the listener. Recent tools reduce this, so it is a mov
nodes.api: console.debug(new Error()) with a getter on Error.prototype.stack; any accessor that fires only when Runtime.enable serializes the object

nodes.p: CPU family (x86 or ARM) and 32 or 64 bit, via high-entropy Client Hints.
nodes.m: Reveals Apple Silicon or Windows on ARM vs Intel or AMD, and bitness. Useful to serve the right binary or WebAssembly build; also splits users into hardware cohorts.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Device class list: Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, XR, Automotive, EInk, Watch.
nodes.m: Newer replacement for guessing from the mobile flag and screen size. Lets a site serve car, e-reader, VR or tablet layouts. Some users report more than one factor.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Android phone or tablet model name, only when the site asks.
nodes.m: Exposes the exact handset (Pixel 8, SM-S928B). Informs device-specific bugs and ad targeting. iOS never exposes a model; desktop returns an empty string.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Exact operating system version, via a high-entropy Client Hint.
nodes.m: Only way left on Chromium to tell Windows 10 from 11 (major 13 or higher means 11) or macOS 14 from 15. Lets sites ship OS-specific features or target upgrade prompts.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: canPlayType and isTypeSupported answers across dozens of codecs.
nodes.m: Pattern of supported codecs (H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9, AC-3, Opus, FLAC) separates browser build and OS. Chrome without proprietary codecs and Chromium builds stand out.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Old non-standard strings naming the CPU class and operating system CPU.
nodes.m: cpuClass (old Internet Explorer) and oscpu (Firefox) mostly return nothing in Chrome, which is itself a signal for which browser engine runs.

nodes.n: CSS system colors and system fonts
nodes.p: Computed values of system color keywords and font names reveal OS and theme.
nodes.m: getComputedStyle on keywords like ActiveText, Canvas, ButtonFace, and system-ui fonts returns OS-specific RGB values and font names. CreepJS uses them to detect OS, theme and spoofing.
nodes.api: getComputedStyle(el).color for system keywords; font: caption, menu, status-bar
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: RAM in gigabytes, rounded down to a power of two and capped at 8.
nodes.m: Lets a site serve a light page to low-memory phones. Rounded to 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 or 8 GB, so a 32 GB workstation and an 8 GB laptop look identical.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Heuristics that guess when the browser developer tools are open.
nodes.m: Used by anti-scraping and anti-cheat code. Methods: window outer minus inner size over about 160 px, console getter traps, debugger timing. Easily false-positive when docked or zoomed.
nodes.api: outerWidth - innerWidth, console.log getter, debugger timing
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Detects installed Chrome extensions by fetching their exposed files.
nodes.m: Learns which extensions the person runs: job tools, ad blockers, accessibility aids, religious or political filters. LinkedIn probes about 6,236 IDs, mapping the result to a named member.
nodes.api: fetch('chrome-extension://<32-char-id>/<file>') succeeds only if exposed via web_accessible_resources; DOM scanning for injected IDs
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A browser that has never been used looks empty in many small ways.
nodes.m: A fresh profile starts with no cookies, empty storage, a history length of one, no earlier permission choices and no extensions. A person's browser rarely looks like that. Cloud browser agents often start from a clean profile each run, so they look like first time visitors. Saving and reusing a profile between runs mak
nodes.api: history.length; document.cookie; localStorage.length; navigator.storage.estimate(); Notification.permission; navigator.permissions.query()

nodes.p: Lists connected game controllers, but only after a button press on the controller.
nodes.m: Reveals a controller is plugged in or paired (id string includes vendor and product IDs). Hidden until the user presses a button, so it is not a silent probe.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Number of logical processors the browser may use.
nodes.m: Splits users into low, mid and high end hardware (2, 4, 8, 12, 16 or more threads). Sites use it to size worker pools; trackers use it as a stable hardware trait.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A few page details look odd when a browser has no real window or desktop.
nodes.m: Older headless Chrome showed an empty plugin list, no languages, a zero outer window size and a notification setting that disagreed with the Permissions API. New headless mode closed most of these gaps. A software graphics renderer and a default 800 by 600 window can still stand out.
nodes.api: navigator.plugins.length; navigator.languages; window.outerWidth; Notification.permission vs permissions.query({name:'notifications'}); WebGL renderer; window.chrome

nodes.n: Headless label in the browser identity
nodes.p: The browser's name tag can say it is running without a screen.
nodes.m: Headless Chrome announces itself as HeadlessChrome in the User-Agent string and in the Sec-CH-UA brand list unless the operator overrides it. Bot defenses read it first. Agents that patch the user agent often forget the client hint brands, so the two disagree and give the agent away.

nodes.p: Infers whether the browser is in a private or incognito window.
nodes.m: Sites use it for metered paywalls and fraud scoring. Browsers keep closing the leaks (quota size, filesystem API, IndexedDB errors), so any method has a short life.
nodes.api: navigator.storage.estimate() quota, IndexedDB open errors, FileSystem API, timing
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Detects which fonts are installed by measuring text width, no permission needed.
nodes.m: Shows OS, office suites and design tools installed (Adobe, Microsoft Office add fonts). FingerprintJS tests dozens of fonts against 3 fallbacks; list entropy was 13.9 bits in 2016.
nodes.api: canvas.measureText(), offsetWidth of spans per font-family
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Which video and audio formats decode smoothly and power-efficiently on this device.
nodes.m: Reveals hardware decoder generation, HDR support and codecs (AV1, HEVC, VP9, Dolby) and so GPU and OS tier. Sites use it to pick streams; it also fingerprints the device.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Counts of cameras, microphones and speakers, without names, before any permission.
nodes.m: Tells a site whether the device has a camera and mic and how many outputs. Without permission labels and device IDs are empty, but kinds and counts leak a hardware profile (laptop vs headset vs desktop).
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.n: Legacy navigator properties (appName, appVersion, platform, vendor ...)
nodes.p: Frozen strings such as appName, appVersion, appCodeName, platform, product, productSub, vendor and vendorSub.
nodes.m: Mostly frozen for compatibility, but platform and vendor still differ by OS and engine. Used for consistency checks against the user agent.
nodes.api: navigator.appName, appVersion, appCodeName, platform, product, productSub, vendor, vendorSub
nodes.dm: Legacy navigator properties (appName, appVersion, platform, vendor ...)

nodes.p: Legacy engine strings: oscpu (Firefox), vendor, vendorSub, productSub, cpuClass.
nodes.m: Quick tells for the rendering engine and OS. vendor is Google Inc., Apple Computer, Inc. or empty (Firefox); productSub is 20030107 on Chromium and Safari, 20100101 on Firefox. Used to catch spoofed browsers.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Legacy string naming the OS family such as Win32, MacIntel, Linux x86_64 or iPhone.
nodes.m: Coarse OS signal that is deprecated but still returned. Often frozen to a fixed value (Win32 on 64-bit Windows, MacIntel on Apple Silicon), so it carries little entropy but reveals spoofed user agents when it disagrees.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Whether the browser shows PDFs inline instead of downloading them.
nodes.m: A single boolean that replaced plugin enumeration. False on some mobile browsers and on users who disabled the viewer. Low entropy but common in bot checks.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Chromium reports JavaScript heap size limits, which track device RAM.
nodes.m: jsHeapSizeLimit is about 2 to 4 GB on 64-bit desktops and 0.5 to 1 GB on low-end phones, bucketed in Chrome, so it hints at RAM class even though deviceMemory is capped at 8.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: List of browser plugins and MIME types; now a fixed list of 5 PDF viewers.
nodes.m: Once the strongest fingerprint (15.4 bits, Flash and Java era). Since Chrome 94 and Firefox 99 it returns a hardcoded PDF list, so it now mostly flags headless or odd browsers.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Flags telling whether the page is HTTPS and isolated from other origins.
nodes.m: isSecureContext and crossOriginIsolated are set by the site itself, so they mostly describe the page, not the person. They gate high-power APIs and timer precision (5 microseconds when isolated, 100 microseconds otherwise in Chrome).
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Installed text-to-speech voices, which reveal OS, version and installed language packs.
nodes.m: macOS lists 100+ voices, Windows 10 to 30, Android per Google TTS pack. Exact list shows OS version and which languages the person installed, a strong stable fingerprint.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Reports how much storage the origin may use, which tracks total disk size.
nodes.m: Chrome and Safari set the quota near 60% of total disk, so quota reveals disk size within a few GB, and Incognito shows a much smaller number. Also usage shows how much the site has already stored.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Tests whether cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB work.
nodes.m: Four booleans plus openDatabase and addBehavior legacy checks. Almost always all true, so low entropy, but they flag locked-down privacy modes and blocked storage.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: How many simultaneous touches the screen supports and whether touch events exist.
nodes.m: Separates phone and tablet from desktop, and touch laptops from plain ones. maxTouchPoints is 0 on mouse-only devices, 5 on most phones, 10 on many tablets and touch PCs.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Detailed device and browser versions a site can request with Accept-CH or a JavaScript call.
nodes.m: Returns exact OS version, CPU, bitness, device model and full browser version. Not sent unless the site asks. The browser can decline, but Chrome currently answers without a prompt.
nodes.api: navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues([...]); Accept-CH response header then Sec-CH-UA-* request headers
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Browser brand list, mobile flag and OS name that Chromium sends by default.
nodes.m: Three coarse hints (Sec-CH-UA, Sec-CH-UA-Mobile, Sec-CH-UA-Platform) replace most of the old User-Agent. They split the audience into mobile vs desktop and Windows vs macOS vs Android with almost no tracking power.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: The browser's self-description sent on every request and readable in JavaScript.
nodes.m: Tells the site browser brand and major version, OS family, and CPU family. Used for compatibility and bot filtering. Since UA reduction the string is coarse, so finer detail moved to opt-in Client Hints.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: The text the browser sends naming its browser, version and operating system.
nodes.m: Says which browser, version and OS the person uses. Chrome has been reducing detail since 2022, but the string still gates features, and LinkedIn's extension probe only runs when it contains Chrome.
nodes.api: navigator.userAgent; User-Agent header; UA Client Hints

nodes.p: True when the browser is being driven by Selenium, Playwright, Puppeteer or similar.
nodes.m: Tells a site a script, not a person, may be on the page. Bot defenses use it with other tells (missing plugins, headless UA) to block or challenge scrapers and agents.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Tells whether the browser is controlled by automation, plus other marker checks.
nodes.m: True for Selenium, Puppeteer and similar. LinkedIn also looks for PhantomJS and Selenium markers on window and document.
nodes.api: navigator.webdriver; window._phantom, window.callPhantom, document.__selenium_unwrapped and similar

nodes.p: About 65 WebGL limits and an extension list that differ by GPU and driver.
nodes.m: MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE (4096 to 32768), MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS, shader precision formats and supported extensions together fingerprint the GPU even when the renderer string is hidden.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Reads the graphics card and driver name through WebGL.
nodes.m: Exposes GPU model and driver (ANGLE (NVIDIA, GeForce RTX 4070 ...)). Identifies the device tier and OS. Safari reports a generic Apple GPU; Brave and Firefox spoof or trim it.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: GPU vendor, architecture, features and limits through WebGPU.
nodes.m: adapter.info gives vendor and architecture (nvidia, ampere); Chrome blanks device and description by default. Limits (maxTextureDimension2D 8192 or 16384) and the feature list still tier the GPU.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Lets a page ask what each permission is currently set to without prompting.
nodes.m: navigator.permissions.query() returns granted, denied or prompt for most permissions. It reveals which permissions you have granted or blocked, and a change event lets pages react live.
nodes.ui: No prompt; read only. States: granted, denied, prompt. A permissions policy block reports denied.
nodes.ps: n/a

nodes.p: HTTP header and iframe allow attribute that decide which features a page or frame may use.
nodes.m: Lets a site disable features for itself and its iframes. MDN lists 51 directives; each can be self, a list of origins, or none. A feature blocked here never reaches the user prompt.
nodes.ui: Server sent header plus iframe allow attribute; cross-origin frames get a feature only if both parent and frame allow it.
nodes.ps: Per document

nodes.p: Sites cannot scan for nearby Bluetooth devices without a picker you approve.
nodes.m: Web Bluetooth (Chromium) requires a user gesture, a chooser prompt and a service filter; the page only gets devices the person picks. Silent scanning does not exist. Safari and Firefox do not support Web Bluetooth.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Sites cannot read your bookmarks or reading list.
nodes.m: Only browser extensions with the bookmarks permission can read them. A web page has no API at all; even installing a PWA is detectable only through display-mode.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Sites cannot read which other sites you visited.
nodes.m: :visited styling is limited since Chrome 51 and Firefox 4 (getComputedStyle lies, only color changes) so history sniffing no longer works. Proxies: cache timing, HSTS and partitioned storage are now keyed per site, and referrer shows only the prior page.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Web pages cannot read calls, texts or messages on the device.
nodes.m: No browser API exposes call history or SMS inboxes. WebOTP reads a single matching code. Android native apps need READ_SMS and READ_CALL_LOG; Google Play restricts both heavily.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Sites cannot read your mobile carrier, SIM or tower ID.
nodes.m: Only the Network Information type (cellular) on Android Chromium and the server-side IP to ASN lookup reveal the carrier (about 100 major carriers). No MCC, MNC, SIM or tower API exists on the web.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

f.n: proxy: IP to ASN lookup (server side)

nodes.p: Sites cannot read your address book; they only see contacts you pick.
nodes.m: The Contact Picker (Android Chrome 80, Chrome iOS no) returns only the entries the person ticks, per call. No bulk read exists, unlike native apps that hold the contacts permission.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: No API reads CPU heat; only coarse pressure buckets exist.
nodes.m: Compute Pressure API (Chrome 125, secure context) returns nominal, fair, serious or critical, throttled to at most 1 update per second and capped per origin. Exact degrees, fan speed and wattage are not exposed. Battery level is separate.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.n: Serial number, IMEI and device ID
nodes.p: Sites cannot read your serial number, IMEI or advertising ID.
nodes.m: No unprompted API exposes hardware identifiers. Managed ChromeOS and enterprise policies expose serial to allowlisted extensions only (chrome.enterprise.deviceAttributes). A regular site gets none; fingerprints are rebuilt from many signals instead.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

f.n: proxy: Web Bluetooth or WebUSB serialNumber

nodes.p: Exact free disk space is hidden; a fuzzy quota estimate leaks.
nodes.m: navigator.storage.estimate().quota is about 60% of disk in Chrome and Safari 17, with noise. Exact free space and total disk size are not exposed; quota gives bits of a size class (256 GB vs 512 GB vs 1 TB).
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Only a capped RAM figure exists; exact memory is hidden.
nodes.m: deviceMemory returns 0.25 to 8 GB (capped, Chromium, secure context, power of two rounding), so a 64 GB workstation looks like 8. Firefox and Safari expose nothing. Memory pressure is not readable.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Sites cannot list your folders or see where files live.
nodes.m: The File System Access API (Chromium) returns handles after a picker; the real path is withheld (fakepath). OPFS is a private sandbox. Only the file name, size and last modified are readable.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A site cannot list your installed apps, except to check its own related app.
nodes.m: navigator.getInstalledRelatedApps() (Chrome Android 80, Chrome desktop 140 for PWAs) only answers for apps declared in the site manifest related_applications. Custom URL scheme probing is blocked or prompts. Roughly 0 bits for arbitrary apps.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: iOS Safari hides the exact device model.
nodes.m: The UA says only iPhone or iPad with a frozen OS string. Proxies: screen size (390x844 etc.) and DPR narrow to a generation, and WebGL renderer says Apple GPU. Exact model such as iPhone 15 vs 16 is often ambiguous, about 2 to 3 bits.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

f.n: proxy: screen width x height, dpr

nodes.p: A page cannot read your device's network hardware address.
nodes.m: MAC addresses never reach the web platform. Proxies are weak: WebRTC local candidates (mDNS now) and Bluetooth device IDs after a prompt are per-origin and randomized. iOS and Android also randomize Wi-Fi MACs per network.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Pages cannot see your computer login name.
nodes.m: No web API exposes it. Proxies: file-picker display names after the user chooses a file, a downloaded file path in a native dialog, and rare leaks in error messages from extensions or file:// URLs.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A page cannot see what other tabs show, only whether its own tab is visible.
nodes.m: Same-origin policy and site isolation block it. Proxies: Page Visibility and focus say if this tab is hidden, BroadcastChannel talks to same-origin tabs, and Window Management lists screens (prompt). Number of open tabs is unknown.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A page cannot read the phone number of your phone or SIM.
nodes.m: No web API returns the device's own number. Proxies: WebOTP reads an SMS code (needs a prompt-free user flow but only the code, only formatted for the origin), Credential Management and Contact Picker give numbers the person chooses.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A page cannot learn your real IP if a VPN works properly.
nodes.m: Servers see the VPN exit IP. Leaks come from WebRTC (local IPs now hidden by mDNS), DNS leaks outside the browser, IPv6 bypass and timezone or language mismatch. Browsers expose no 'real IP' API.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Pages cannot read passwords or addresses saved in the browser.
nodes.m: Password managers fill on user action or after an autofill choice. Known weak spot: hidden-field autofill attacks and the :autofill CSS pseudo-class, which reveals that a field was autofilled (a boolean), but never the value before user action.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: A site cannot read how bright your screen is set.
nodes.m: No API exposes backlight level. Proxies: prefers-color-scheme, dynamic-range and Screen Wake Lock state. Ambient light sensor was removed from stable browsers (Chrome behind a flag, Firefox 122 removed it) for fingerprint and privacy risk.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: No API tells a page how loud the device volume is.
nodes.m: Volume is OS state. Proxies exist: autoplay policy shows a muted tab, audio output device changes fire devicechange, and a muted video can still play. A page cannot read a 0 to 100 level.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.n: Wi-Fi name, BSSID and signal strength
nodes.p: Sites cannot read your Wi-Fi network name, router ID or signal bars.
nodes.m: Wi-Fi identity is a location tracker (BSSID databases map to street addresses). Browsers expose none of it. Proxies: Network Information type on Android, server-side IP geolocation, and the Geolocation API which uses Wi-Fi servers behind its prompt.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Fetches a hidden file from each of thousands of known extension IDs to learn which ones are installed.
nodes.m: Reveals installed add-ons, which can imply job search, sales role, religion, health or politics, and a stable identifier for the browser profile. LinkedIn calls it abuse prevention; critics call it covert profiling.
nodes.api: fetch('chrome-extension://<id>/<file>') per list entry, Promise.allSettled; fulfilled = installed
nodes.ps: Runs on page load for every visit; result is sent once per run if any ID is found
nodes.dm: Set of installed extension IDs out of the probe list
nodes.du: every page load or session start

nodes.n: Spectroscopy DOM scan for extension traces
nodes.p: Walks the page's own DOM looking for chrome-extension:// strings that extensions inject.
nodes.m: Finds extensions that modify the page even when they hide their files from fetch probes. A passive second way to learn which add-ons the person runs while using the site.
nodes.api: recursive DOM walk (scanDOMForPrefix) over text nodes and attributes; SpectroscopyEvent
nodes.ps: Per page; cookie spectroscopyId is session scoped

nodes.n: Color depth, pixel depth and pixel ratio
nodes.p: Reads bits per pixel and the device pixel ratio (zoom or Retina factor).
nodes.m: Pixel ratio shows Retina screens and browser zoom. Together with resolution it identifies display class.
nodes.dm: Color depth, pixel depth and pixel ratio

nodes.p: Bits per pixel the screen reports; almost always 24.
nodes.m: Reported colorDepth is 24 on nearly everything (30 on some wide-gamut Safari setups, 16 or 32 rarely). Low entropy but included in every library.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Widest color space the screen shows: sRGB, P3 or Rec2020.
nodes.m: P3 separates Apple devices and OLED phones from budget screens. A few bits of hardware signal.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Replaces the mouse pointer with an image, or hides it, inside the page.
nodes.m: A site can change or hide the pointer, helping games and drawing apps. Browsers block cursors that could imitate system pointers or hide over browser UI, so a page cannot fake the cursor outside its own area.
nodes.api: CSS cursor: url(img) x y, auto; cursor: none
nodes.ps: Per element, while the pointer is over it; no stored state
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: How many physical pixels per CSS pixel; also changes with browser zoom.
nodes.m: Values like 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.625, 3 reveal retina screens, Windows scaling and the person's zoom level (50% to 500%). Zoom shifts DPR so it leaks accessibility settings.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: How the page is shown: browser tab, standalone, fullscreen, PWA.
nodes.m: Shows the app was installed as a PWA and whether the person runs it in a window. Useful for install analytics.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Opens a small always-on-top window containing any HTML.
nodes.m: Floats custom page content above other windows (video call controls, timers). A page can keep a floating surface visible while you work elsewhere, so it can also be abused for fake UI.
nodes.ui: No prompt; needs a gesture. The floating window shows the origin and is closable.
nodes.ps: Until closed

nodes.p: Whether the screen can show HDR.
nodes.m: Tells a site to serve HDR video. Splits users into standard and HDR displays (modern iPhones, MacBook Pro, HDR monitors).
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: True when Windows High Contrast or similar forces a palette.
nodes.m: Strong accessibility signal (low vision or migraine users). Mostly Windows contrast themes. A tiny share of users, hence very identifying for those who use it.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Lets a page take over the whole screen.
nodes.m: Needs a click or tap and shows an exit hint. Fullscreen can hide the address bar, which scam pages abuse to fake a browser UI. Esc always exits; iPhone Safari allows only video elements.
nodes.ui: No prompt: transient activation required; browser shows a notice and Esc to exit. Firefox shows a one-time first-fullscreen warning.
nodes.ps: Until exit; ends on tab switch in some browsers
nodes.rv: Esc, F11, tab switch, or swipe

nodes.n: Embed another page in an iframe
nodes.p: A page can show another site inside a frame unless that site blocks framing.
nodes.m: A site can embed a third party page (maps, video, ads, payment forms) and, if it frames you without protection, overlay invisible content for clickjacking. Framing headers and sandbox settings control who can do this.
nodes.api: <iframe src sandbox allow>; Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors; X-Frame-Options
nodes.ps: While the frame is on the page; the framed site's own cookies may be blocked as third party
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: True if the OS inverts colors (Safari Smart Invert).
nodes.m: Accessibility setting visible only in Safari and WebKit browsers. Used by FingerprintJS as a Safari-only trait.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Lets a fullscreen page capture shortcut keys like Esc, Alt+Tab or Ctrl+W (Chromium only).
nodes.m: A site can keep keys the browser or OS would normally take, which remote desktops, games and cloud IDEs need. It also lets a hostile fullscreen page swallow the usual escape shortcuts for a moment.
nodes.ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
nodes.ps: Ends on unlock(), leaving fullscreen or navigation; nothing is stored
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Whether the screen is portrait or landscape and its rotation angle.
nodes.m: Shows how a phone is held and whether a tablet is docked. Reports type (portrait-primary etc.) and angle 0, 90, 180 or 270; changes with a rotate event.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.n: Page zoom: read it, restyle it, intercept the shortcuts
nodes.p: Reads how zoomed the page is, zooms its own content, and can swallow the zoom shortcuts, but cannot set the browser zoom itself.
nodes.m: A page can notice browser zoom (the pixel ratio and window size change, and a resize event fires), zoom its own elements with CSS, and intercept Ctrl+wheel and Ctrl plus, minus and zero before the browser acts. It can also switch off pinch zoom on touch screens with the viewport meta tag. It cannot change the real brow
nodes.api: devicePixelRatio, visualViewport.scale, resize event, CSS zoom, wheel and keydown preventDefault, meta viewport user-scalable and maximum-scale
nodes.ps: Only while the page runs; the browser keeps its own zoom per site
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Pops a video into a small always-on-top window, usually after a click.
nodes.m: A site can float a video above all other apps, which keeps attention on its content while the person works elsewhere. The person can close or resize it, and a site cannot place or hide the window.
nodes.ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
nodes.ps: Ends on exit, video unload or navigation; nothing is stored
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Whether the main input is a mouse, finger or stylus and whether hover works.
nodes.m: pointer is coarse for touch, fine for mouse or pen; hover is hover or none. any-* variants say if any attached device qualifies, revealing a mouse on a tablet or a touchscreen on a laptop.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Whether the OS or browser theme is light or dark.
nodes.m: Reveals the person's OS appearance setting (dark mode is used by an estimated 40 to 60% of mobile users) and time of day if auto switching. Low entropy; often set at the site by cookie.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: OS setting for higher or lower color contrast.
nodes.m: Signals low vision or light sensitivity. Values no-preference, more, less, custom. Rare, so each non-default value is highly distinguishing.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: User wants less data use (data saver).
nodes.m: Pairs with Save-Data. Still behind a flag in Chrome, so almost always no-preference.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: OS setting to reduce animation.
nodes.m: Marks people with vestibular disorders or motion sensitivity (a health-adjacent setting). Roughly 5 to 15% enable it (estimates differ by platform).
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: OS setting to reduce translucent effects.
nodes.m: Accessibility and low-vision hint. New and rare.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Estimated by timing animation frames; 60, 90, 120 or 144 Hz.
nodes.m: No API reports refresh rate; scripts measure the gap between requestAnimationFrame callbacks. Distinguishes high-refresh phones and gaming monitors, but is noisy under load.
nodes.api: requestAnimationFrame timestamp deltas over about 1 second
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Offsets between full screen and usable area reveal taskbar or dock size and position.
nodes.m: Shows macOS dock height and side, Windows taskbar edge, notches and system bars. Identifies OS UI settings and multi-monitor layout. Firefox now hides taskbar size by default.
nodes.api: screen.availTop, availLeft, availWidth, availHeight vs width, height
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Reads portrait or landscape and angle.
nodes.m: Shows how the phone or tablet is held and whether a laptop screen is rotated.

nodes.p: visualViewport reports pinch-zoom scale and on-screen keyboard offsets.
nodes.m: Scale above 1 tells the person is zoomed in (accessibility); height shrink exposes the on-screen keyboard. Updates live as the user pinches or types.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: The monitor or phone screen size in CSS pixels, plus the usable area.
nodes.m: Identifies device model families (iPhone 390x844) and monitor setups (1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3440x1440). Safari 26 and Firefox protections spoof or round it for known scripts; Firefox RFP returns the window size.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Moves the page scroll position and can change scrolling behaviour or capture the wheel.
nodes.m: A site can jump the page, animate scrolling, restore position or block back-bounce. That helps navigation but also supports scrolljacking and trapping scroll inside a panel.
nodes.api: window.scrollTo({top, behavior}); history.scrollRestoration='manual'; overscroll-behavior; wheel listeners
nodes.ps: Per page view; scrollRestoration is a per entry setting
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Tints the browser's address bar or tab strip with a color the page picks.
nodes.m: A site can suggest a colour for the browser toolbar to match its brand. The tag is write only: it reveals nothing about the person, and the browser may ignore it.
nodes.ps: Per page; the browser re-reads it on navigation or when the tag changes
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Screen refresh type, whether JS is enabled, and monochrome depth.
nodes.m: update is none for e-ink or print; scripting reports enabled or none; monochrome is 0 on color screens. Mostly identifies e-readers and print contexts.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Keeps the screen from dimming or sleeping while the tab is visible; no prompt.
nodes.m: A site can stop the screen going dark, which is useful for recipes, maps and video, but drains battery. The browser drops the lock the moment the tab is hidden, so it cannot run in the background.
nodes.ps: Released when the tab is hidden, the sentinel is released, or the page closes; must be requested again after a visibilitychange
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Asks to see all connected monitors and place windows on them.
nodes.m: Reveals how many screens you have, their sizes, positions, labels and scale. That is a strong device fingerprint and lets a site open fullscreen windows on a chosen monitor.
nodes.ui: Chrome prompt: Manage windows on all your displays, Allow or Block. screen.isExtended is readable without a prompt.
nodes.ps: Persistent per origin
nodes.dm: ScreenDetails with one ScreenDetailed per monitor

nodes.p: Moves or resizes a popup the site opened; ignored for normal tabs.
nodes.m: A site can reshape a popup it created, but the browser blocks changes to tabs and pre-existing windows, so scripts cannot yank your main window around or hide it off screen.
nodes.api: win.moveTo(x, y); win.resizeTo(w, h); win.moveBy(dx, dy)
nodes.ps: Per window; applies once, no stored state
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Window position on the desktop and whether more than one monitor is attached.
nodes.m: screenX and screenY can reveal monitor layout; screen.isExtended says if a second display exists, without a prompt. Detailed monitor list (getScreenDetails) does need a permission.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Browser window and viewport dimensions, which change constantly.
nodes.m: Reveals tiling, maximized vs windowed use, sidebars and devtools. Firefox RFP rounds inner size to 200x100 steps (letterboxing) so everyone shares a few buckets.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Makes a temporary URL for in-memory data or a File, usable in links, images and downloads.
nodes.m: A site can hand files to itself without a server round trip. The URL works only in that browser and origin and dies when the page unloads or is revoked.
nodes.ps: Until the document unloads or revokeObjectURL() is called
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.n: Capture attribute (camera or mic from a file input)
nodes.p: Opens the phone camera or microphone directly from a file input; the page gets one finished file.
nodes.m: A site can skip the gallery and ask for a fresh photo, video or recording. It gets a single file, not a live stream, and the person confirms each capture.
nodes.ps: Per capture
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.n: File System Access: folder picker and blocked folders
nodes.p: Lets the person grant a whole folder for reading and writing; sensitive system folders are refused.
nodes.m: A folder grant shares every file inside it and lets the site edit them. Chrome refuses root, system and the profile home folders so one click cannot expose the whole disk.
nodes.ui: Chrome folder picker, then View files and Save changes bubbles
nodes.ps: Handle storable in IndexedDB; permission per session or persistent in Chrome 122
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Lets the person pick a whole folder; the page gets every file in it with relative paths.
nodes.m: One pick shares a full folder tree, often thousands of files. The site sees file names and sub folder structure, so a careless pick can expose more than expected.
nodes.ps: Per selection
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.n: Dropping files and folders onto the page
