nodes.m: Sizes of text and emoji boxes depend on installed fonts, text shaping, zoom and OS, giving a hash that works even when canvas is blocked.
nodes.dm: Floats with up to 10 decimal places per measurement

nodes.p: Renders emoji and rare Unicode characters and measures or hashes how they look.
nodes.m: Each OS and version ships a different emoji font and Unicode level, so the rendered glyph set pins the OS, its version and sometimes the vendor skin on Android.
nodes.api: canvas fillText('emoji'); measureText(); DOM span width
nodes.dm: Pixel or width signature of 20 to 100 Unicode samples

nodes.p: Triggers errors and reads their message text and stack trace format.
nodes.m: Error wording and stack layout differ between V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore, and shift per version, revealing real engine under a spoofed user agent.
nodes.api: try { null.x } catch(e){ e.message, e.stack }; Error.captureStackTrace; Error.stackTraceLimit

nodes.p: Tests hundreds of font names by comparing text width against a fallback font.
nodes.m: Installed fonts reveal OS, Office or Adobe apps, languages and sometimes profession (design, dev). The list is stable and shared by few people, one of the strongest fingerprint inputs.
nodes.dm: Probe 100 to 1,000 font names, 1 bit each (installed or not)

nodes.p: Measures text width to guess which fonts are installed.
nodes.m: Font lists reflect installed apps, languages and OS version. Flash font enumeration was another method before Flash ended in 2020.
nodes.api: Measure text in offscreen elements; Flash getFontList (obsolete)

nodes.p: Times many identical GPU draw calls to expose per-chip speed differences.
nodes.m: Manufacturing variation in execution units makes even identical GPU models slightly different. DrawnApart separated identical GPUs after only 150 ms of drawing and remained stable for weeks.
nodes.api: WebGL drawArrays loops; performance.now(); WebGPU compute

nodes.p: Reads Intl resolved options and formatting outputs for many locales and calendars.
nodes.m: Beyond timezone and language, ICU data version, supported calendars and numbering systems differ per browser build and OS, enabling version and cloak detection.

nodes.n: JS and Web API feature detection (version pinning)
nodes.p: Checks which JavaScript, WebAssembly and Web APIs exist to estimate the exact browser version.
nodes.m: New APIs appear on known dates, so a map of 200 to 1,000 properties pins the version within 1 to 2 releases and exposes bots, spoofed user agents and privacy modes. Client Hints and UA reduction make this the main version signal.

nodes.p: Evaluates Math.tan, cosh, expm1 and similar at odd inputs and compares the exact digits.
nodes.m: JS engines and CPU math libraries round the last bits differently, so a few results separate V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore and sometimes the OS and CPU architecture.

nodes.p: Asks which audio and video codecs, containers and DRM systems the browser supports.
nodes.m: Hardware decoders for HEVC, AV1 and DRM (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady) differ by OS and chip, so the map reveals device class and licensing.
nodes.dm: Bit vector plus power efficiency flags

nodes.p: Lists installed plugins and supported MIME types.
nodes.m: Once a strong fingerprint. Since Chrome 94 the list is a fixed set of PDF viewers, so it now adds little.

nodes.p: Lists the text-to-speech voices installed on the device.
nodes.m: Voices reveal OS, installed languages, downloaded premium voices and Google or Microsoft cloud voices, which hints at language and accessibility use.

nodes.p: Measures SVG text extents and glyph positions.
nodes.m: SVG layout uses a separate text path from HTML, so metrics add fonts and rasterizer detail even under HTML-layout defenses.

nodes.p: Detects when privacy tools or anti-detect browsers have replaced browser functions.
nodes.m: Checks native toString, prototype descriptors and cross-signal consistency (WebGL renderer versus user agent). Finds noise injection, so being protected becomes a fingerprint of its own.

nodes.p: Reads the GPU vendor and model string, hardware limits and the list of supported WebGL extensions.
nodes.m: Exposes the exact GPU model and driver family (for example 'ANGLE (Apple, M2)'), which is a strong device class signal and reveals gaming, laptop or phone hardware.
nodes.dm: About 70 numeric limits plus 30 to 40 extension names

nodes.p: Renders a fixed 3D scene with custom shaders and hashes the output pixels.
nodes.m: Floating point and rasterization differences across GPU, driver and ANGLE backend produce a hash that separates devices better than the renderer string, even hardware with the same label.
nodes.dm: Hash of the framebuffer, typically 256x128 px

nodes.p: Reads float and integer precision ranges the GPU shader units support.
nodes.m: Mobile GPUs report different mediump and highp precision, so the numbers separate desktop, Apple, Adreno, Mali and PowerVR families.

nodes.p: Reads the graphics card name and GPU capability values.
nodes.m: Reveals the GPU vendor and model and a set of limits, which together identify a hardware class and often a precise device.

nodes.p: Asks the browser which GPU vendor and architecture WebGPU will run on.
nodes.m: Returns vendor, architecture and sometimes device and driver description, a cleaner GPU label than WebGL's masked string. Chrome rounds it, but features and limits still expose the hardware tier.

nodes.p: Reads which optional WebGPU features and numeric limits the GPU supports.
nodes.m: About 30 limits and 15 optional features (for example shader-f16, timestamp-query) form a fine-grained hardware and driver signature, usable for model-size gating and for fingerprinting.
nodes.dm: About 30 integer limits and up to 20 feature flags

nodes.n: Apple Pay and Private Click Measurement flags
nodes.p: Safari-only flags: Apple Pay availability and ad attribution support.
nodes.m: ApplePaySession.canMakePayments reveals whether Apple Pay is set up on the device (a financial hint) and PCM support marks Safari. Both are tested by FingerprintJS.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: AudioContext.baseLatency reveals the audio stack and hardware.
nodes.m: Typical values 0.005 to 0.04 seconds depending on OS and driver (macOS about 0.01, Windows 0.01 to 0.03, Android up to 0.04). Mild hardware signal; read without playing sound.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Telling ARM from x86 by how Float32 values behave in JavaScript.
nodes.m: FingerprintJS writes a Float32Array and reads bytes to detect endianness-like behavior. Chromium reduced UA hides CPU, but such probes can infer the architecture class anyway.
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.p: Tiny differences in Math.tan, acosh, sinh and others across engines and CPUs.
nodes.m: Results of about 10 transcendental functions differ in the last digits between V8, SpiderMonkey, JavaScriptCore and OS math libraries. Identifies engine version and sometimes CPU family. Firefox 145 made some math more uniform.
nodes.api: Math.acos(), asinh(), atanh(), expm1(), log1p(), sinh(), tan(), pow() ...
nodes.ps: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored

nodes.n: APFC / DNA device fingerprint (abuse prevention features)
nodes.p: Collects about 48 device and browser traits, encrypts them, and attaches them to later requests.
nodes.m: Builds a device fingerprint from hardware, display, locale, rendering and storage traits. Because it is encrypted with a LinkedIn key and sent as a header, people and researchers cannot easily see what leaves the browser.
nodes.api: Fingerprint2.js derived collector; RSA encrypt (key apfcDfPK); compressToBase64; globalThis.apfcDf; header on API calls; /platform-telemetry/li/apfcDf, /apfc/collect
nodes.ps: Cookies li_bapfcc and li_odapfcc 2 years (control how many features are collected); li_apfcdc 10 hours (triggering)

nodes.n: Battery Status API and drain inference
nodes.p: Reads battery level, charging state and time estimates in Chromium browsers.
nodes.m: Level and discharge time can short-term link visits across sites. Remaining time infers device load. Removed from Firefox and never added to Safari because of the tracking risk.
nodes.api: navigator.getBattery(); BatteryManager level, charging, chargingTime, dischargingTime

nodes.p: Times how fast a resource loads to guess whether the person already visited a site.
nodes.m: A cached image or script loads in milliseconds, an uncached one in tens. Probing resources from other sites, or the status of a login, reveals browsing history. Cache partitioning mostly ended the cross-site variant.

nodes.p: Reports the device CPU load as nominal, fair, serious or critical.
nodes.m: A PressureObserver reports coarse CPU state and thermal throttling (four levels), limited to secure contexts and top level or permission policy frames. Replaces CPU benchmarking for adaptive apps, but exposes load state.

nodes.p: Runs short compute loops to estimate how fast the device is.
nodes.m: A 50 to 500 ms JS or WebAssembly benchmark, plus worker scaling to test the real core count, ranks a phone or laptop into speed tiers. Used for adaptive quality, bot detection (headless VMs) and as a fingerprint component.
nodes.api: performance.now() loops; Worker pools; WebAssembly; Atomics
nodes.dm: Elapsed ms per benchmark, noise 2 to 10%

nodes.p: Sites that send COOP and COEP headers unlock finer timers and SharedArrayBuffer.
nodes.m: Gives a page a 5 microsecond clock and shared memory, both needed for wasm threads. A worker counter on SharedArrayBuffer is a high resolution clock that also powers Spectre-class attacks.

nodes.n: Clock skew and crystal timing fingerprint
nodes.p: Measures tiny clock speed differences between a device's timers.
nodes.m: Each device has slightly different oscillator frequencies. Comparing performance.now, Date, requestAnimationFrame and server timestamps over many seconds yields a device-specific drift signature, researched as time-based fingerprinting.

nodes.p: Measures how long clicks, taps and key presses take to produce the next frame.
nodes.m: Records each interaction's input delay, processing time and presentation delay (8 ms granularity) so sites can compute Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and also learns when and how fast people interact.
nodes.dm: Entries with startTime, processingStart, duration (rounded to 8 ms)

nodes.p: Tells whether the person has clicked or typed recently, and in Chromium whether they are idle.
nodes.m: navigator.userActivation shows if a click or key happened. IdleDetector (permission gated, Chromium) reports user active or idle and screen locked. Without it, sites infer idle from the absence of input events.
nodes.dm: userState: active or idle, screenState: locked or unlocked

nodes.p: Records key press and release times to build a typing rhythm profile.
nodes.m: Dwell times (key held) and flight times (between keys) for password and free text identify people with 1 to 5% error. Persists across devices and accounts, used for continuous authentication and fraud.

nodes.n: Paint timing (FCP, LCP) and Core Web Vitals
nodes.p: Reports when content first appeared and the largest element rendered.
nodes.m: PerformancePaintTiming and LargestContentfulPaint give render timings that reflect network, CPU and GPU. Cross-origin images need Timing-Allow-Origin for full detail.

nodes.p: Reports frames that took over 50 ms and which scripts caused them.
nodes.m: Shows slow frames with script URLs, durations, forced layout and blocking time. Gives site owners (and third party scripts) a view of device speed and which embedded scripts exist on the page.

nodes.p: Asks for a breakdown of memory the page and its iframes use.
nodes.m: Reports total bytes and per-origin attribution in cross-origin isolated contexts. A noisy but accurate measure of memory use, useful for leaks and for inferring device memory pressure.

nodes.n: Microarchitectural timing attacks (Spectre, DrawnApart, cache side channels)
nodes.p: Uses precise timing to read CPU cache or GPU execution quirks.
nodes.m: Browser JS can run cache side channels (prime+probe), Spectre variants and GPU timing fingerprints (DrawnApart, 2022) that identify a physical GPU by execution unit speeds. Defended by timer coarsening and site isolation.
nodes.api: performance.now(), SharedArrayBuffer clocks, WebGL/WebGPU timer queries

nodes.p: Records cursor paths, speed and acceleration.
nodes.m: Movement curvature, jitter and click timing separate humans from bots and can identify repeat users. Coalesced events give up to 1000 Hz traces on gaming mice.

nodes.p: Reports DNS, connect, TLS and download timings for the page and each resource.
nodes.m: Reveals connection speed and CDN behavior, whether a request hit the cache, protocol (h2, h3) and TLS reuse. Cross-origin detail needs the Timing-Allow-Origin header, otherwise sizes and phases are zeroed.
nodes.dm: One entry per resource, about 20 timestamps each

nodes.p: Exposes estimated connection type, speed and data saver preference.
nodes.m: navigator.connection returns effectiveType (4g, 3g...), rtt rounded to 25 ms, downlink rounded to 25 kbps steps (max 10 Mbps) and saveData. Chrome on Android adds type (wifi, cellular); other browsers do not support it.
nodes.api: navigator.connection.effectiveType, rtt, downlink, saveData; Save-Data and Downlink request headers

nodes.p: Tells a page when its tab is hidden, backgrounded or unfocused.
nodes.m: Sites learn when the person switches tabs, minimizes or locks the screen. Used for attention tracking, exam proctoring and ad viewability, and by bot detectors that expect focus events.

nodes.p: Reads JavaScript heap sizes in Chrome.
nodes.m: Exposes usedJSHeapSize, totalJSHeapSize and jsHeapSizeLimit, which cluster by device RAM and OS (about 4 GB on 64-bit desktop, 2 GB on mobile). Values are quantized.

nodes.p: Counts animation frames per second to find the monitor's refresh rate.
nodes.m: requestAnimationFrame timing reveals 60, 90, 120, 144 or 165 Hz displays, and variable refresh. Combined with devicePixelRatio and screen size it narrows the device model (e.g. ProMotion iPads and iPhones at 120 Hz).

nodes.p: Servers send timing metrics to the page through a response header.
nodes.m: Lets a backend or CDN expose database, cache and edge timings to client JavaScript, for monitoring or for leaking server state when cross-origin readable.
nodes.dm: Each metric name plus dur in ms

nodes.p: performance.now() returns a clock whose coarseness depends on browser and isolation.
nodes.m: Timer resolution is a deliberate defense against timing attacks. The resolution itself tells a site the browser and whether privacy mode or cross-origin isolation is on, and limits attacks like cache timing.

nodes.p: Records scroll speed, swipe shape and touch pressure and size.
nodes.m: Touch events expose contact radius, rotation and force (where hardware supports it); scroll and swipe timing is device and person specific. Used in mobile behavioral biometrics and bot checks.
nodes.api: touchstart/touchmove Touch.radiusX, rotationAngle, force; scroll events; PointerEvent.pressure

nodes.p: Used to detect which links the person had visited by styling :visited links.
nodes.m: Browsers lie to getComputedStyle for :visited since 2010, but timing, scroll and rendering side channels remained. Chrome 136 partitions :visited links, ending cross-site history probing.

nodes.n: OpenTelemetry in the browser (real user monitoring)
nodes.p: A script that packages page timings, network calls and clicks into the OpenTelemetry format and sends them to the site's collector.
nodes.m: OpenTelemetry is not a browser feature. It is an open standard and a set of libraries that a site loads. In the browser it reads the timing APIs the page already has (navigation, resource, paint and user timing), wraps fetch and XHR, and records clicks, then ships it all as traces and metrics. It can also stamp a trace
nodes.api: @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-web with document-load, fetch, xml-http-request and user-interaction instrumentations; OTLP/HTTP exporter (POST /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs)
nodes.ps: Per page; buffered spans are sent with fetch or sendBeacon and nothing is stored in the browser by default
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke; content blockers that block the collector address stop the export
nodes.dm: Spans, metrics and logs with nanosecond timestamps (browser timers are coarsened to about 0.1 ms or more)
nodes.du: Batched, usually every few seconds and on page hide

nodes.p: Tells a page when it is frozen, discarded or restored from the back/forward cache.
nodes.m: A site can see when a tab goes to sleep, was discarded to free memory, or came back instantly from the back button, which reveals how you navigate and how much memory the device has.
nodes.api: pageshow, pagehide, freeze, resume, document.wasDiscarded, visibilitychange
nodes.ps: Per page; state follows the lifecycle events until the page is discarded
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.n: Reporting API (crash, CSP and deprecation reports)
nodes.p: Sends the browser's own error, crash and policy violation reports to a site endpoint.
nodes.m: A site can learn when its page crashes, runs out of memory, hits a blocked resource or uses a deprecated feature on your device, and gets those reports even after the page closed. No prompt is shown.
nodes.ps: Reports are queued and sent in the background, even after the tab is closed
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Runs code before each screen refresh, and reveals the display's refresh rate.
nodes.m: A site can learn your monitor's refresh rate (60, 120, 144 Hz) by counting frames, and can tell when the tab is hidden because callbacks stop. It is the core of smooth animation.
nodes.ps: Per page; callbacks run once per display refresh while the tab is visible
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Runs low priority work when the browser is idle; no prompt.
nodes.m: A site can wait until the page is quiet before running analytics or prefetching. It also reveals roughly how busy your device is, since idle windows are shorter on slow devices or busy tabs.
nodes.ps: Per page; callbacks do not run when the tab is in the background in most engines
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)

nodes.p: Records the browser's clock value when collection starts.
nodes.m: Time value used to order events and to check clock drift against the server.

nodes.p: Lets a page stamp named points in time and measure the gaps between them.
nodes.m: A site can time its own code in detail and send the numbers home, so it learns how fast the person's device and network really are. The marks live only in this tab and are not shared across sites.
nodes.ps: Per page; entries are in memory until the page closes or clearMarks is called
nodes.rv: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
